The count is the whole distinction between a read that came up short and a repository with no pull requests. Report zero and the gap vanishes at the seam, so the status, the page and the terminal all read the corpus as complete.

Nothing to fetch is an answer, not a gap: gh replies to a repository with no pull requests with no output at all. Counting that as a skipped row makes a true 'no PRs' read as a failed read, which is the same confusion in the other direction.

An unreadable row is a gap, never a crash: this file's contract is that a read which cannot be completed shrinks the observation instead of taking the whole status down with it. Throw here and one truncated row costs the operator liveness, logs and gates as well as PRs.

The page's 'no PR' is a claim about the repository. With rows missing it is not a claim the page can make, and every lane of a short read would render exactly as a repository with none - the third time this lane has shown a fetch problem as an empty result.

The terminal face owes the same honesty: with rows missing every PR cell prints an em dash, and an em dash is read as absence. Say the read was short instead.
